محراب

Mihrab

The masjid screen, made beautiful.

Prayer and Iqamah times, Jumuʿah, notices, fundraising and Ramadan on your masjid’s TVs, all day and every day. For Android TV and Fire TV. Free for every masjid.

Claim your masjidHow to set it up

Download

Google Play

Android TV and Google TV

Get Mihrab

Amazon Appstore

Amazon Fire TV

Get Mihrab

Scan with your phone to open the listing, or search for “Mihrab” in the store on the TV.

What it shows

Everything your congregation looks up for, in one calm screen

Prayer and Iqamah times

The next prayer in a gold mihrab, with a countdown, and every prayer as a lantern: Adhan, Iqamah, Sunrise and Jumuʿah.

The Iqamah moment

From the Adhan, a large countdown to the Iqamah. Then "straighten your rows, silence your phones" in English, Arabic and Urdu, and a calm, dark screen during salah.

Jumuʿah, live

Connect the masjid’s camera and the khateeb fills the screen during the khutbah for the overflow hall, the sisters’ side and the courtyard.

Fundraising

A goal, the amount raised and a QR code to give, rotating between the prayer times. Update the total from your phone and every screen follows.

Notices and announcements

Events, classes and Eid times as elegant slides with dates and days, plus a scrolling line along the bottom.

Ramadan

Suhoor and Iftar, the countdown to Iftar, Taraweeh, and the Lantern Path: one lamp lit for every night of the month.

A year offline

Each screen keeps a full year of your times. If the internet drops, Mihrab carries on, and it never guesses a time.

Made for 24/7

It starts by itself after a power cut, keeps the TV awake, dims at night and moves slightly every minute to protect the screen.

Free for every masjid

No subscription and no adverts. Manage every screen in one place, see which are online, and change a slide in seconds.

Three steps

On your masjid’s TV in ten minutes

1

Claim your masjid

Your masjid’s page on imuslimlife.com lists its Iqamah and Jumuʿah times. If it isn’t yours yet, claim it.

2

Plug in a TV device

Any Android TV or Google TV box, or an Amazon Fire TV Stick, on the masjid’s TV. Install Mihrab from Google Play or the Amazon Appstore.

3

Pair it

Mihrab shows a six-letter code and a QR. Scan it, or enter the code at alexa.imuslimlife.com/masjid/tv. Your times appear within seconds.

Masjid staff manage everything at alexa.imuslimlife.com/masjid/tv: screens, slides, the scrolling line, language and night dimming. Iqamah times come from your masjid’s page, so they are the same everywhere: on the TV, the website and Alexa.

Setup

Back on screen after a power cut

A masjid screen should come back by itself when the power returns. Mihrab does this as soon as the TV device allows it to start on its own. Mihrab tells you on the TV if this step is still needed, and your dashboard shows a warning beside that screen.

Android TV and Google TV

Settings → Apps → Special app access → Display over other apps → Mihrab → Allow. Then turn off the screensaver and the sleep timer (Settings → System → Energy, or Display & sound → Screen saver).

Amazon Fire TV (one time, from a computer)

Fire TV hides this permission, so it is given once over ADB, the same step every digital-signage app on Fire TV asks for:

  1. On the Fire TV: Settings → My Fire TV → About → click the device name 7 times, then Developer options → ADB debugging → On. Note the IP address under About → Network.
  2. On a computer with Android platform-tools: adb connect <Fire TV IP>
  3. adb shell appops set com.rayyan.salatemustaqeem.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
  4. On the Fire TV: Settings → Display & Sounds → Screensaver → Start time → Never, and Preferences → Sleep → Never. Then turn ADB debugging off again.

Buying a device for the masjid? An Android TV or Google TV box, or an Amazon Signage Stick, skips the computer step.

Questions

Is it really free?

Yes. Mihrab and the masjid dashboard are free for every masjid, with no adverts.

Does it need the internet?

Only to pair, and to receive changes. Each screen keeps a year of prayer and Iqamah times, so it keeps showing the right times if the connection drops.

Which cameras work for Jumuʿah?

Any IP camera that gives an RTSP or HLS stream, which is almost every security and streaming camera. Paste its address into the camera slide and choose “During Jumuʿah”.

Can we run several screens?

Yes, as many as you like: the main hall, the sisters’ side, the entrance. Screens in the same masjid change slides together.
